page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.12xlarge is a dedicated high-performance computing instance driven by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with a 24-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The system provides 24 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring consistent per-core execution. The processor includes a 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 768 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 5 GHz, translating to an allocation of 32 GB per core. The instance is provisioned without local storage disks or GPU accelerators, but it incorporates an exceptionally high 300 Gbps network interface baseline.

Empirical benchmarks reflect strong performance characteristics in memory throughput and multi-core calculations. The instance achieves top-decile large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 635.15 GB/s and write bandwidth of 377.27 GB/s, matching the requirements of memory-starved simulation loops. Compute testing shows strong results, including a multi-core stress-ng score of 73603.42, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 16049.0, and a PassMark CPU metric of 50953.52. High-throughput decompression tests also register in the top quartile, with multi-threaded bzip3 achieving 314.52 GB/s. PassMark database tests reach 24969.18 operations, while web serving and single-threaded operations align with middle-tier baseline levels.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high per-core RAM density and high-speed networking against the absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated graphical processing units. Workloads that depend on low-latency local disk caching must access networked volumes over the 300 Gbps fabric, which offers the throughput needed to prevent network I/O bottlenecks. In terms of cost efficiency, paying for 32 GB of DDR5 per physical core offers high value for memory-bound simulation codes, but represents resource surplus if deployed for simple compute workloads that do not leverage its extreme memory footprint or multi-hundred gigabit network tier.

Given its dedicated core pinning, extensive DDR5 bandwidth, and 300 Gbps network interface, the hpc7a.12xlarge is structured for parallel engineering and scientific workloads. Key target applications include computational fluid dynamics, structural analysis, climate modeling, reservoir simulation, distributed molecular dynamics, and large in-memory analytical pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.12xlarge is a high-performance computing instance built on the AWS Nitro system, combining compute power with large memory capacity. It is powered by a 24-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz with dedicated physical cores and single-threading. The instance integrates 768 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory, yielding an expansive 32 GB of RAM per core, alongside a high-throughput 300 Gbps network baseline. It contains no local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits top-tier uncached memory read bandwidth of 635.15 GB/s and write bandwidth of 377.27 GB/s, coupled with strong multi-core computational throughput and solid database operations. Its resource allocation favors compute-intensive and memory-bound jobs that require massive throughput across nodes without hyperthreading interference. This configuration is well matched for computational fluid dynamics, weather modeling, finite element analysis, large-scale simulations, and memory-heavy scientific data processing pipelines.
